Seminar Title:

Evolution of the Dalma meta-igneous suite and associated felsic rocks: implications for the tectonic history of the North Singhbhum Mobile Belt, Eastern India

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Earth and Atmospheric Sciences

Speaker Name:

Adyasha Pati ( Rollno : 524er1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Room No: ER-303, Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences

Date and Time:

13 Oct 2026 16:30

Contact:

Rekha S.

Abstract:

The Dalma meta-igneous suite of the North Singhbhum Mobile Belt (NSMB) represents an important Mesoproterozoic mafic magmatic belt whose tectonic evolution remains poorly understood. This study integrates field geology, structural analysis, petrography, mineral chemistry, and metamorphic pressure-temperature estimates to characterize the lithological, structural, and metamorphic evolution of the suite. Field investigations show that the Dalma meta-igneous suite is composed predominantly of foliated mafic to ultramafic rocks, whereas granitoids and supracrustal rocks occur to the north and south. Three generations of planar fabrics (S1, S2, and S3) were observed, with S2 representing the dominant regional foliation and S1 occur as relict within S2. The S2 foliation exhibits variable orientations and is folded into open to tight folds with gently plunging fold axes. A later, penetrative S3 foliation, striking ~ E&ndashW, having steep dips and steeply plunging fold axes transposes S2. Petrographic observations reveal mineral assemblages comprising hornblende, plagioclase, chlorite, epidote-clinozoisite, quartz, titanite, and ilmenite, together with locally preserved hornblendeand plagioclase-rich globular domains interpreted as relict igneous features. Mineral chemistry identifies hornblende and actinolite amphiboles, albite-andesine plagioclase, and clinochloreripidolite chlorite. Amphibole-plagioclase thermometry and amphibole barometry yield metamorphic conditions of 450&ndash660 &degC and 6&ndash12 kbar, whereas hornblende-rich globular domains record 580&ndash660 &degC and 5.5&ndash10.8 kbar. These P-T estimates indicate metamorphism under amphibolite-facies conditions. Chlorite thermometry yields estimated temperatures of approximately 250&ndash400 &degC, indicating low- to moderate-temperature metamorphic and/or retrograde hydrothermal conditions. Geochemical analysis of the rocks suggests mafic, tholeiitic and low-K basaltic compositions with oceanic-arc/subduction-related affinities, indicating a depleted mantle source modified by subduction-derived components. Traceelement and Mg# trends further suggest fractional crystallization involving olivine/pyroxene and plagioclase. The integrated dataset demonstrates that the Dalma meta-igneous suite preserves evidence of multiple deformation events, regional metamorphism, and localized high-strain zones, providing new constraints on the tectonic evolution of the NSMB.
